title: Bounded Initial Configuration
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $\text{orc}$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four indices and each Boolean word, and let $M\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory marking. Suppose a machine state $st$ has all 17 register values at most $B$, and an integer $p$ satisfies $0\le p\le P$. Then, for every program label $l$, the configuration with label $l$, registers from $st$, no answer yet, memory $M$, and memory head at $p$ satisfies the invariant: its instruction safety condition holds, all register values are at most $B$, and the head lies between $0$ and $P$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: Each of the 17 register values in $st$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $K_0,B,P\in\mathbb N$, let $x$ be a bit string, and let $M:\mathbb
Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. If every one of the 17 register values in a state
$S$ is at most $B$, and the memory-head position $p$ satisfies $0\le p\le P$, then, for
every program label $l$, the configuration with label $l$, register values from $S$,
empty answer, memory $M$, and head at $p$ satisfies the invariant $G(x,B,P)$.
